body: claimed: mkinney (Claude agent, M3) · 2026-11-09T17:52Z · plan: research (no branch) - published approaches to on-machine probing as coordinate measurement (feature measurement, form/position from touch points, compensation/uncertainty), what CamCraft already has (Probe op, G31/G38 hooks, macro reads), what is required vs reasonable, and a proof-of-concept proposal; findings posted here

## Research: using the touch probe as a CMM (on-machine measurement)

Research only: no code, no branch. Sources are public standards (catalogue pages and public summaries; the normative texts are paywalled), vendor **public** application notes and control manuals (read for behaviour only), and published literature. No Autodesk Fusion or HSMWorks material or output was consulted, and no other CAM system's output was either. Sources are listed at the end and referenced as [S#].

### TL;DR

- **It is feasible and worth doing, but call it on-machine *verification*, not a CMM.** The machine that cut the part also measures it, so its own geometric errors largely cancel out and stay invisible. The probing standard itself says it does **not** assess a machine tool used as a CMM, and points to the CMM standards (ISO 10360-2/-5) for that [S1].
- **What it catches well:** setup and fixturing errors, tool deflection and wear, a wrong tool offset, a missing pass, and gross size or position errors. **What it cannot certify:** absolute accuracy, form at the micron level, or anything that has to pass an inspection sign-off.
- **CamCraft already has about half of the pipeline:** a Probe op that knows each touch's nominal contact, pick-to-feature seeding, a stylus collision law, and posts that emit G31 or G38.2 and capture trips into macro variables. **The missing half** is: more than 4 touches per feature, getting the trips *out* of the control and back into CamCraft, fitting, comparing against the model, and a report.
- **Proof of concept:** measure one bore (8 touches) and one top face (9 touches) on the Tormach with G38.2. Log each trip with LinuxCNC's `LOGOPEN`/`LOG` (or `PROBEOPEN`), import the log, fit a least-squares circle and plane, and report the deviation from the model. Details and a sub-issue split are below.

---

### 1. What CamCraft has today (survey of `main` plus open PRs)

| Piece | Where | What it does | Gap for CMM use |
|---|---|---|---|
| Probe op | `crates/app/src/operation/probe_op.rs`, `crates/motion/src/probing.rs` (`ProbeParams`, `ProbeMode`) | Modes are Face, Edge, Corner, Bore and Boss. Bore and Boss use **4 fixed touches** (±X, ±Y). Fast and slow feeds, approach, overtravel, backoff, `tolerance`, and an optional `set_wcs` (G54..G59) | Point counts are fixed (4 points on a circle leaves 1 redundant degree of freedom, so form cannot be judged). Touches run only along X, Y or −Z. Every op is a "find and maybe set the WCS" op; there is no "measure only, keep every point" op. |
| Probe from pick (#171) | `probe_pick.rs`, `probe_pick_round.rs` | Seeds the op from a picked face, edge, vertex or round wall. The round seed takes centre and radius from the circle fit (`circle_of_region`). | This is already the **measurement plan from model features** step, with nominals. It only needs to emit N points instead of 4. |
| Protected-move law (#108, #172) | `stylus_hits`, `stylus_reach_hits` | The ball, stem and body are swept against the model. A stylus driven into material is refused as a gouge. | Reusable as is for N-point patterns. |
| Intermediate stream | `crates/post/src/post/probe_rec.rs` | `TOUCH target expect F [measure k]`, `RETREAT delta`, `FOUND axes, mean, expected, tolerance` | Each touch already carries its **nominal** (`expect`) and a measurement index `k`, which is exactly the key a results log needs. |
| Fanuc post | `assets/posts/fanuc.cps` `onProbeMove/onProbeRetreat/onProbeResult` | G31 skip, then `#5061..#5063` into `#(100+3k)..`, a no-contact alarm, the deviation into `#190..`, an out-of-tolerance alarm `#3000`, and an optional `G10 L2` | The result **stays on the control**. Nothing is written out. |
| Tormach post | PR #376 (open, #362) | G38.2, then `#5061..#5063` into `#(100+3k)`, with `(MSG, ...)` and a G10 L20/L2-style WCS update | Same: nothing leaves the control. |
| Haas, Mazak, Siemens | PR #360 (open, #173) | Probing hooks | Same. |
| Inverted X/Y | PR #465 (open, #392) | `post::invert` mirrors TOUCH, RETREAT and FOUND (`S = −1` on the inverted axis). It also adds a test-only **macro-B controller** (`crates/app/tests/macro_b/`) that runs posted Fanuc programs and trips G31. | Any results import must undo the same `S` flip. The macro-B test controller is a ready-made **simulator** for producing logs in tests. |
| Lathe "probe ask" (M5.3 D) | `crates/app/src/operation/probe.rs` | A CamCraft-side prediction of what a probe *would* find, before anything runs | It is a prediction, not a measurement. A measured result could later be judged by the same report. |

**What comes back to the app today: nothing.** Trips live in volatile control variables, and the only feedback is an alarm or a WCS update on the machine.

### 2. What a "probe as CMM" pipeline needs

1. **Measurement plan from model features.** Pick a feature (already possible), then generate a touch pattern: N points on a circle at one or more heights (a cylinder), an M×N grid on a plane, and K points on a line. Each touch's nominal contact point and surface normal come from the model. NPL's CMM strategy guide covers point count and distribution per feature type [S10]. Rule of thumb from that literature: the point count should well exceed the minimum (3 for a circle or plane) so that form and outliers are visible.
2. **Touch-point generation.** Approach along the surface normal, which for a bore is radial, not just ±X/±Y. Use the same fast/slow double touch already in the op. Renishaw's public notes show that a single touch at gauging feed on a control with a few milliseconds of scan time can be off by tenths of a mm, while a slow second touch brings that down to microns [S6]. NIST reports the same proportional dependence of trigger-timing error on probing feed [S7]. Every move stays under the protected-move law.
3. **Results capture back into CamCraft.** This is the new mechanism. All of the following are documented:
   - **LinuxCNC / PathPilot:** `(PROBEOPEN file.txt)` stores X Y Z A B C U V W of *every successful straight probe*, and `(PROBECLOSE)` closes the file. `(LOGOPEN,file)`, `(LOGAPPEND,file)`, `(LOG,text with #params)` and `(LOGCLOSE)` give free-form lines with parameter expansion. `#5061..#5069` hold the trip "in the coordinate system in which the G38 took place", and `#5070` holds success/fail for G38.3/.5 [S2][S3]. Caveat: forum reports disagree on whether `LOGOPEN` writes under PathPilot and say PathPilot limits file access, while `PROBEOPEN` was reported to work [S4]. **Step 0 of the PoC is to confirm this on the actual machine.**
   - **Fanuc-style macro B / Haas:** `POPEN` / `DPRNT[...]` / `PCLOS` send formatted text out. Haas documents that DPRNT sends formatted text to the serial port, that POPEN and PCLOS are accepted only for compatibility, and that on NGC Setting 261 chooses the destination (disabled, file or TCP port) [S5].
   - **Heidenhain:** measuring cycles write a log (for example `TCHPR4xx.TXT` beside the program, controlled by `Q281`) with nominals and deviations [S8]. That is a vendor cycle's log; CamCraft would read the format, not reuse the cycle.
   - The **key** that joins a log line to a CamCraft touch is the existing measurement index `k`. Each log line should carry `k`, the op id and the trip XYZ.
4. **Probe compensation.** The reported trip is the position of the controlled point (the ball centre, or the tip, depending on the tool length setup), not the contact point. The standard practice is to **fit the ball-centre points and offset the fitted feature by the effective ball radius**. For a bore, fit a circle to the centres and add r_eff; for a face, fit a plane to the centres and shift it by r_eff along its normal. This avoids needing to know each contact normal. r_eff (and per-direction "lobing" or pre-travel variation) comes from calibrating on a ring gauge or sphere of known size, and is only valid for that stylus, feed and direction set [S9][S7]. CMM practice derives the effective tip radius the same way, from a certified sphere [S9].
5. **Fitting.**
   - Least-squares (Gaussian) fits with orthogonal distance: plane (centroid plus smallest eigenvector of the covariance), line, circle and sphere.
   - For circles, an algebraic fit (Kåsa is fast but biased on short arcs; Pratt, Taubin or "Hyper" are better) seeds a geometric Gauss-Newton / Levenberg-Marquardt refinement [S11][S12].
   - NIST's reference algorithms (Shakarji, ATS) define the expected behaviour and are the basis of ASME B89.4.10 software testing, so they make good test oracles [S12].
   - Minimum-zone (Chebyshev) fits are what form tolerances are strictly defined on (ISO 1101 / ASME Y14.5 tolerance zones [S14][S15]). Least-squares *overestimates* flatness and roundness slightly compared to minimum-zone, which is the conservative direction. Chebyshev can come later.
6. **Comparison to model and tolerances.**
   - Size (diameter), position (centre XY against the model's nominal, in the setup's WCS), form (flatness and roundness as the range of residuals), and plane height and orientation.
   - CamCraft has no PMI (STL, STEP B-rep without GD&T), so v1 tolerances are **user-entered per measured feature**, and the probe op already has `tolerance`.
   - Decisions follow ISO 14253-1: a result within the measurement uncertainty of a limit is *indeterminate*, not a pass [S13].
7. **Report.** A per-feature table (nominal, measured, deviation, tolerance, verdict, and number of points and residual range), plus the raw points. It can sit beside the existing setup-sheet export. The viewport can overlay deviation arrows at each touch.

### 3. Reasonable versus not reasonable (accuracy)

- **The same machine is both instrument and producer.** A scale or squareness error in an axis is in the cut and also in the measurement, so it cancels and is never seen. Thermal growth during the cycle, and the gap between measuring the part warm and clamped versus cold and released, add further errors [S7][S16]. That is why ISO 230-10 tests the *probing system* on the machine and explicitly defers "machine as a CMM" to ISO 10360-2/-5 [S1].
- **What a real CMM has that we don't:** a controlled environment, a traceable, verified volumetric error (ISO 10360-2 length error and ISO 10360-5 probing error, the 25-point sphere test with the range of radii as P_FTU [S17]), and a qualified stylus.
- **Ways to recover some trust (all reasonable later):**
  - Ring-gauge or sphere calibration of r_eff at the measuring feed and directions.
  - A double touch at a slow second feed.
  - **Substitution or comparator measurement** in the style of ISO 15530-3: measure a calibrated master part like the workpiece on the same machine with the same program, and correct by the difference. This is the documented way to get task-specific uncertainty from a non-CMM [S18].
- **Verdict:**
  - *Reasonable:* in-process verification ("is the bore within ±0.02 of nominal, is the face where the model says, did the finish pass leave stock"), re-work decisions, setup checks, and trend logging.
  - *Not reasonable:* certifying parts, judging form tighter than the machine's own repeatability, or presenting numbers as CMM-equivalent. The report must say "on-machine measurement - not a CMM result" and show the uncertainty the user states, never one we invent.
  - *Order of magnitude (our estimate, not sourced):* on a prosumer mill like the Tormach, trust measurements to roughly the machine's stated positioning repeatability plus the probe's stated repeatability, both from the user's own manuals.

### 4. Proof of concept (smallest useful slice)

**Target:** a Tormach (PathPilot, G38.2). It measures one through-bore (8 points at one height) and the top face (3×3 grid), compares them to the model, and prints a report.

**Step 0, mechanism check (manual, before any code).** Run a hand-written program on the machine (and in a stock LinuxCNC sim) to confirm which logging path PathPilot honours, and where the file lands:

```
(PROBEOPEN probe485.txt)          ; documented: one XYZABCUVW line per successful G38.2
(LOGOPEN,probe485-log.txt)        ; documented: free-form, #param expansion
G38.2 X.. Y.. F..                 ; fast touch (G38.2 itself errors if nothing trips)
G91 G1 X-1 F..  G90               ; incremental backoff, as the post does today
G38.2 X.. Y.. F..                 ; slow touch
(LOG,T 1 7 #5061 #5062 #5063)     ; op 1, touch k=7, trip in the program's WCS
...
(LOGCLOSE)
(PROBECLOSE)
```

If LOGOPEN is dead on PathPilot, use PROBEOPEN (positional order, so k is the line index of the slow touches) or `(DEBUG,...)` as a last resort. Record the result on this issue.

**Steps 1-4 (code):**
1. **Inspect pattern** in the Probe op: `points: N` for Bore and Boss (radial approach at N equal angles) and a grid for Face (−Z). Set `set_wcs` to none and add a "measure only" flag so no alarm or WCS write is posted. Seeding from a pick (#171) and the stylus law come for free.
2. **Tormach post:** when the op is measure-only, wrap it in `LOGOPEN`/`LOGCLOSE` (or `PROBEOPEN`/`PROBECLOSE`). After each slow TOUCH, emit `(LOG,T <op> <k> #5061 #5062 #5063)`. Golden NC in `tests/golden/nc/tormach/`.
3. **Import:** a command `ImportProbeResults { op, file }` (undoable, per "Everything Is a Command"). It parses the lines, converts units (PathPilot may run G20), maps WCS to the model frame through the setup's WCS origin and `Location`, applies the inverted-axis `S` flip (#392), and joins on `k` to each touch's nominal. Malformed, missing or duplicate `k` values are refused by name, and the importer never crashes.
4. **Fit and report:**
   - Circle: Kåsa seed, then Gauss-Newton geometric fit on the ball centres, plus r_eff.
   - Plane: centroid plus eigenvector, shifted by r_eff.
   - Report diameter, centre XY deviation, roundness (residual range), plane Z deviation, flatness and tilt against the model's nominals, with a user tolerance and stated uncertainty, as a text/CSV table in the Probe op panel.
   - Tests use synthetic points (with known noise) and the macro-B / G38.2 simulator from PR #465 to produce logs end to end.

**PoC done means:** on the Tormach, a part with a known reamed bore and a faced top yields a report where bore Ø agrees with a bore gauge or pin gauge, and face Z with the DRO touch-off, within what the user judges reasonable for that machine. In CI, the same pipeline on simulated trips recovers a planted 0.05 mm centre offset and 0.02 mm oversize to within 1 µm.

### 5. Proposed sub-issues (each `enhancement`, `source:agent`, "Part of #485")

1. **Geometry: least-squares fits for plane, line, circle and sphere** (`area:geometry`, P2). Orthogonal-distance fits in `camcraft-geometry` (algebraic seed, then geometric refinement), returning parameters, residuals and range.
   - *Done means:* NIST-style synthetic sets (exact points, noisy points, partial arcs ≥ 90°) are recovered to 1e-9 exact and within the expected noise. Degenerate input (fewer than the minimum points, collinear points for a plane or circle, NaN) returns an error and never panics.
2. **Probe op: measure-only N-point patterns** (`area:probe`, P2). `points` for Bore and Boss (radial approach), an M×N grid for Face, a measure-only flag (no WCS write, no tolerance alarm), the stylus law applied to every touch, and pick seeding.
   - *Done means:* an 8-point bore and a 3×3 face generate, are judged by `stylus_hits`/`stylus_reach_hits`, and round-trip through the project file. Existing 4-touch ops are unchanged (golden NCs identical).
3. **Post: probe result logging, Tormach/LinuxCNC** (`area:post`, P2; stacks on PR #376). `LOGOPEN`/`LOG`/`LOGCLOSE` (or `PROBEOPEN`) per measure-only op, one line per slow touch keyed by op and `k`. Step 0's mechanism check is recorded first.
   - *Done means:* a golden NC, plus the log format documented beside `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md`.
4. **Post: probe result output, Fanuc/Haas macro B** (`area:post`, P2). `POPEN`/`DPRNT[T*<op>*<k>*#100[44]...]`/`PCLOS`, with the destination stated in the setup sheet (Haas Setting 261).
   - *Done means:* golden NCs for Fanuc and Haas, and the macro-B test controller from PR #465 executes DPRNT into a captured log.
5. **App: import probe results** (`area:app`, P2). An undoable `ImportProbeResults` command that parses LinuxCNC and DPRNT logs, handles units, maps WCS to the model frame, applies inverted-axis `S`, joins on `k`, and stores measured points on the op (freed when the op is deleted).
   - *Done means:* the import → undo → redo test passes. Malformed, partial or foreign logs are refused with a diagnostic (fuzz test). A G20 log and an inverted-X log map to the correct model points.
6. **App/UI: measurement report** (`area:ui`, P2). Per-feature fit (via sub-issue 1) with r_eff compensation, deviation from model nominal, user tolerance and stated uncertainty, an ISO 14253-1-style pass/fail/indeterminate verdict, a panel table plus CSV export, and the banner "on-machine measurement - not a CMM result".
   - *Done means:* a synthetic end-to-end test recovers the planted deviations, and a UI snapshot shows the table.
7. **Probe calibration on a ring gauge or sphere** (`area:probe`, P2, after 2-5). A calibration op (N-point bore on a gauge of entered certified Ø) that yields r_eff (and per-direction pre-travel), stored on the probe tool and used by sub-issue 6.
   - *Done means:* simulated trips with a planted per-direction pre-travel give back r_eff and per-direction corrections, and sub-issue 6 uses the tool's r_eff.
8. **Later, `needs-research`:** minimum-zone (Chebyshev) form evaluation [S12]; cylinder and multi-level patterns; ISO 15530-3-style master-part substitution [S18]; MTConnect or TCP result pull instead of files.

Suggested order: 1 → 2 → 3 → 5 → 6 makes the PoC on the Tormach. 4 and 7 follow, and 8 stays research.

### Sources

- [S1] ISO 230-10:2022, *Test code for machine tools — Part 10: Determination of the measuring performance of probing systems of numerically controlled machine tools* (scope: does not assess the machine tool as a CMM; refers to ISO 10360-2/-5). https://www.iso.org/standard/78909.html
- [S2] LinuxCNC documentation, *G-code Overview*: Numbered Parameters (#5061-#5070), Probe Logging (PROBEOPEN/PROBECLOSE), Logging (LOGOPEN/LOGAPPEND/LOGCLOSE/LOG), Comment Parameters. https://linuxcnc.org/docs/html/gcode/overview.html
- [S3] LinuxCNC documentation, *G-codes*, "G38.x Straight Probe". https://linuxcnc.org/docs/html/gcode/g-code.html#gcode:g38 , and NIST RS274NGC Interpreter v3 (NISTIR 6556). https://www.nist.gov/publications/nist-rs274ngc-interpreter-version-3
- [S4] LinuxCNC forum, *smartprobe - configuration questions* (user reports on PROBEOPEN and LOGOPEN under PathPilot; anecdotal, to be verified in Step 0). https://forum.linuxcnc.org/38-general-linuxcnc-questions/31077-smartprobe-configuration-questions?start=10 , and Tormach, *CAM driven probing*. https://knowledgebase.tormach.com/770m/cam-driven-probing
- [S5] Haas Automation, *Communication with External Devices - DPRNT* (DPRNT formatted output; POPEN/PCLOS kept for compatibility; NGC Setting 261 output to file or TCP). https://www.haascnc.com/service/troubleshooting-and-how-to/how-to/communication-with-external-devices---dprnt.html
- [S6] Renishaw, white paper TE412, one-touch versus two-touch probing, scan time and measurement uncertainty (listed under *Technical papers*). https://www.renishaw.com/nl/technical-papers--15963 ; companion TE413 *Optimising measurement cycle time*. https://renishaw.com/resourcecentre/en/download/white-paper-te413-optimising-measurement-cycle-time--33648
- [S7] A. V. Ling, N. D. Wilkin, *Fast Probing Considerations for On-Machine Inspection of Parts*, NISTIR 6415 (1999). https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/Legacy/IR/nistir6415.pdf
- [S8] HEIDENHAIN iTNC 530 *Touch Probe Cycles* user manual (measuring cycles 4xx, Q281 measuring log). https://content.heidenhain.de/doku/tnc_guide/pdf_files/iTNC530/340490-xx/en/tchprobe.pdf
- [S9] Renishaw, *Innovations in touch-trigger probe sensor technology* (pre-travel variation / lobing, compensated by calibration). https://renishaw.com/resourcecentre/en/download/white-paper-innovations-in-touch-trigger-probe-sensor-technology--4626 , and Transcat, *Qualification sphere calibration* (effective tip radius from a certified sphere). https://transcat.com/qualification-sphere-calibration-quality-assurance-cmm-probe
- [S10] D. Flack, *CMM Measurement Strategies*, NPL Measurement Good Practice Guide No. 41. https://www.npl.co.uk/resources/gpgs/cmm-measurement-strategies

- [S12] C. M. Shakarji, *Least-Squares Fitting Algorithms of the NIST Algorithm Testing System*, J. Res. NIST 103(6) (1998). https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4890955 ; minimum-zone / Chebyshev reference work by the same author: https://www.nist.gov/node/741806
- [S13] ISO 14253-1:2017, *GPS — Inspection by measurement of workpieces and measuring equipment — Part 1: Decision rules for verifying conformity or nonconformity with specifications*. https://standards.iteh.ai/catalog/standards/iso/db344fb2-cbb5-448c-b097-6a81d6e4414d/iso-14253-1-2017 ; UKAS LAB 48 *Decision rules and statements of conformity*. https://ukas.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/LAB-48-Decision-rules-and-statements-of-conformity.pdf
